artist.name: Tony Fomison
artist.bio: Anthony Leslie (Tony) Fomison was a notable artist in New Zealand. He was an important post-war visual artist in the country and influenced New Zealand art by incorporating elements of narrative and myth into contemporary art.

summary:
Australia is navigating a complex mix of economic challenges and significant scientific and legal milestones. While rent growth has stalled for stretched tenants and the RBA signals potential rate hikes, there is notable progress in healthcare access, with pharmacy availability of the abortion pill jumping nearly 50% following regulatory easing. A landmark High Court ruling has also strengthened environmental protections by requiring planning authorities to consider overseas fossil fuel emissions, a victory for Hunter Valley residents. In the realm of science, an Australian-led trial has found promising evidence that an experimental drug could lessen brain inflammation in people at high risk of Parkinson’s, offering hope for slowing the disease’s progression.

Internationally, the focus remains on resilience and human achievement. In Nepal, the government has shifted from search and rescue to rehabilitation for those impacted by devastating floods, highlighting a constructive response to disaster. Meanwhile, in the United States, thousands of volunteers have joined the American Red Cross to provide immediate relief, demonstrating the power of community solidarity. Scientific breakthroughs continue to advance globally, including the discovery of the first known microblazar by astronomers and a Nobel Prize in chemistry awarded for resolving mirror images in chemical molecules, a discovery that has transformed modern medicine.

Cultural and social stories also highlight human connection and agency. In Australia, Cricket Australia is actively reviewing the women’s schedule in response to player concerns, signaling a commitment to equity in sport. Internationally, the merger of Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery is reshaping Hollywood, while in France, student protests have led to a suspension of stun grenade use, reflecting a dialogue on public safety. These stories collectively emphasize the ongoing efforts of communities, scientists, and policymakers to address challenges with innovation, care, and collective action.

sources.title: Community solidarity after the floods - Friends of the Earth Australia
sources.snippet: Among the harrowing stories of loss and destruction, there are many of mutual aid, solidarity, empathy and bravery. As author Rebecca Solnit explained so beautifully in her book ‘A Paradise Built in Hell’, during and after disasters, it is the self initiative and self organising of affected communities that does some of the best work at emergency relief and long term recovery. As the clean up gets underway, here are some ideas of local initiatives you may want to support. Image: Aidan and Tim rescuing their neighbours in Lismore (Eddie Lloyd)

sources.title: AJEM January 2025 - Embedding humanity in building sustainable community disaster resilience in Australia: a humanistic communication perspective | Australian Disaster Resilience Knowledge Hub
sources.snippet: Such an approach to resilience entails recognising evolving and diverse human needs and mobilises human subjectivity and agency in co-developing disaster resilience. Philosophically, the approach advocated is underpinned by ‘critical humanism’ theory. Guided by foundational conceptual positions, a model of humanistic communication that introduces principles of humanity (i.e. connectivity, diversity, interactivity) into the disaster cycle to foster community engagement and empowerment is proposed.
